correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge2\), the source substitution is a bijection of the ordered positive chamber. After the source prefactor \(\sqrt{q_1}\), its Jacobian is \(w_1/\sqrt{w_1^2+(q_1-1)w_2^2}\), strictly below one when \(q_1>1\). The transformed coefficient sequence has prefix sums \(1,r_2,\ldots,r_n\), so the source prefix argument also makes its Gaussian exponent no smaller than the standard exponent; hence the Jacobian loss yields strictness. Thus equality forces \(q_1=1\). With \(q_1=1\), the exact identity \(\sum_j(q_j-1)z_j^2=\sum_k(r_k-k)(z_k^2-z_{k+1}^2)\) has nonnegative coefficients and strictly positive ordered-square gaps. Any positive prefix defect therefore makes the Gaussian exponent strictly larger throughout the chamber. Equality forces every \(r_k=k\), hence every \(q_k=1\). The orthoscheme conclusion follows from the source identification \(q_j=\beta_j^2\) and its exact quotient reduction. The exceptional \(n=1\) rescaling identity is explicitly excluded from the rigidity claim.

value.rationale: The ordered-square comparison is the central new dimension-free step in the recent proof. Knowing its exact equality locus determines whether the sharp constant can be attained by a nonstandard local orthoscheme: for every \(n\ge2\), it cannot. This isolates the unique local extremal geometry and provides the necessary analytic starting point for any future global rigidity or stability analysis of the sharp surface-area theorem. The dimension-one exception also identifies the precise boundary at which rigidity begins.
